title: Normalized ordinary and derived image data for strict coefficient systems
statement: For the constant quotient-ring strict systems and normalized evaluation package of [lem-pur-coefficient-evaluation-derived-left-adjoint], define the underlying set-sheaf functor, constant-generator maps and scalar-restriction underlying comparison. An ordinary image package consists of normalized algebraic inverse images, right adjoints, scalar-restriction comparisons and exact functors of strict systems with their component adjunctions. A derived image package consists of exact inverse and total right-derived direct images at the system and level categories, normalized chain-map transposes, evaluation, tensor and restriction comparisons with the displayed adjunction-mate and transition equations, joint detection of isomorphisms, lower-bound preservation, and the bounded-below essential-image and normalization criterion. The first six existing declaration bodies are unchanged. The full derived structure groups the same seventeen construction fields into abstract evaluation/scalar data specialized to the prescribed sheaf functors and retains the three formal descent fields. The old twenty projection names remain abbreviations; only the representation changes, not the specified data or equations. The evaluated unit identity is proved from the counit identity and the triangle identities, rather than supplied as independent construction data.

proof.text: The first six definitions are extracted verbatim. Group the construction fields into evaluation data and scalar data over generic abelian categories, specialize every parameter to the prescribed coefficient-system functors, and retain the three formal descent fields. The original seventeen projection names are abbreviations through the grouped construction. No mathematical field or normalization is dropped. Targets using the changed representation require renewed statement review. The formal descent structure is also generic; the public full image abbreviation fixes its direct/inverse functors and its counit-isomorphism and normalization predicates to exactly the original expressions. The evaluation unit equation is a proved theorem: transpose under the level adjunction, precompose with the inverse-evaluation isomorphism, use naturality and the evaluated counit equation, and apply the system triangle identity. It is therefore not an additional construction field.
